blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — For the Subanen people living in Barangay Sipakong, Bacungan, Zamboanga del Norte, getting water for their daily needs used to call for a long walk — 500 meters uphill — to reach springs and other water sources, a journey that took 30 to 45 minutes from the nearest road, depending on the location of their homes. The Subanen people are among the Lumad or Indigenous People of the Zamboanga Peninsula, whose daily struggles with limited or unreliable water supply are further aggravated by a looming Super El Niño.
